reference.source: WHO Guidelines on Leprosy / IADVL Textbook of Dermatology
clinicalPearls: ENL represents a Type 2 lepra reaction, occurring as an immune-complex-mediated (Type III Gell-Coombs) systemic vascular phenomenon
Presents with crops of tender, evanescent, erythematous subcutaneous nodules predominantly on the extensor surfaces of limbs and face
Accompanied by constitutional signs: high fever, arthralgia, lymphadenopathy, neuritis, iridocyclitis, and orchitis
Occurs almost exclusively in multibacillary leprosy (borderline lepromatous and lepromatous leprosy), often triggered by therapy initiation, infection, stress, or vaccination
WHO multidrug therapy (MDT) must continue uninterrupted during an ENL reaction episode
Systemic corticosteroids (oral prednisolone) or thalidomide represent standard medical therapy for severe ENL episodes
Thalidomide is highly effective for recurrent or corticosteroid-dependent ENL in males, but strictly contraindicated in women of childbearing potential due to severe phocomelia teratogenicity
reference.pathophysiology: Erythema nodosum leprosum is a humoral immune-complex (Arthus-type) hypersensitivity reaction triggered by the massive release of Mycobacterium leprae antigens following effective bactericidal therapy. Antibodies bind mycobacterial antigens in circulation and tissues, depositing in vessel walls. Complement activation recruits polymorphonuclear neutrophils, leading to leukocytoclastic vasculitis, acute neutrophilic panniculitis, and intense TNF-alpha, IL-6, and interferon-gamma cytokine release.
additionalDifferentials: Classic erythema nodosum (septal panniculitis without systemic vasculitis or neuritis)
Drug eruptions associated with clofazimine or dapsone
additionalInvestigations: Slit-skin smears for acid-fast bacilli showing granular, fragmented, non-viable forms (lowering of morphological index)
Full-thickness skin punch biopsy demonstrating acute neutrophilic lobular panniculitis with leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Complete blood count showing neutrophilic leukocytosis and elevated ESR/CRP
Renal function tests and urinalysis to detect immune-complex glomerulonephritis or proteinuria
Slit-lamp examination to rule out silent anterior uveitis or iridocyclitis
